prompt:
A six-panel picture-book strip in soft colours with rounded panels, TWO ROWS OF THREE panels. The same three allotment neighbours stand side by side in every panel, all three fully visible: one in a RED coat, one in a GREEN coat, one in a BROWN coat.

WHERE THEY STAND, reading each panel left to right: panel 1 RED, GREEN, BROWN. Panel 2 BROWN, RED, GREEN. Panel 3 GREEN, BROWN, RED. Panel 4 RED, BROWN, GREEN. Panel 5 BROWN, GREEN, RED. Panel 6 GREEN, RED, BROWN.

THE YELLOW PARCEL — exactly one of them is holding it in each panel. In panel 1 it is the person in the RED coat. In every later panel the parcel is in the hands of whoever is now standing immediately to the RIGHT of the person who held it in the previous panel; and if that person is now standing at the far right of the line, the parcel goes instead to the person at the far LEFT. Work out who holds it in each panel — I am deliberately not listing it.

Six different corners of the allotment, a different pose and camera angle each time. No text, no captions, no lettering.
easy_question: This image was supposed to show a comic strip: several separate panels, drawn side by side, with the same small group of people appearing together in each panel. Ignoring artistic quality and ignoring whether the story is right, does the image DEPICT that — a strip of separate panels with a recurring group of figures? A comic page, a storyboard or a picture-book strip all count as yes. Answer NO only if it is blank, a single picture with no panels, or something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.qa: This picture is a comic strip of 6 panels arranged as two rows of three panels. Look at every panel in reading order (the top row left to right, then the bottom row left to right). For EACH panel in that order, report what colour coat the person holding the YELLOW PARCEL is wearing. Use only these words: red, green, brown, blue, white. The people change places from panel to panel, so look at each panel on its own. The panels do not have to agree with one another — report what each panel actually shows, one answer per panel, even if the answer repeats or changes from panel to panel. Answer with exactly 6 answers separated by commas, in panel order, and nothing else.
reference.qa2: The picture is a strip of separate drawings arranged as two rows of three panels. Going through them in the top row left to right, then the bottom row left to right order, tell me, for each drawing in turn, what colour coat the person holding the YELLOW PARCEL is wearing. Allowed answers: red, green, brown, blue, white. The people change places from panel to panel, so look at each panel on its own. Judge each drawing on its own — two drawings may well disagree, so do not assume the strip is consistent. Reply with exactly 6 comma-separated answers and nothing else.
reference.qb: This picture is a comic strip of 6 panels arranged as two rows of three panels. Look at every panel in reading order (the top row left to right, then the bottom row left to right). For EACH panel in that order, report what colour coat the person standing on the LEFT of the panel is wearing. Use only these words: red, green, brown, blue, white. The panels do not have to agree with one another — report what each panel actually shows, one answer per panel, even if the answer repeats or changes from panel to panel. Answer with exactly 6 answers separated by commas, in panel order, and nothing else.
reference.qb2: The picture is a strip of separate drawings arranged as two rows of three panels. Going through them in the top row left to right, then the bottom row left to right order, tell me, for each drawing in turn, what colour coat the person standing on the LEFT of the panel is wearing. Allowed answers: red, green, brown, blue, white. Judge each drawing on its own — two drawings may well disagree, so do not assume the strip is consistent. Reply with exactly 6 comma-separated answers and nothing else.
reference.q_notext: Does this image have any printed number, digit, numeral, written label or caption overlaid on it (as opposed to being purely a photograph / drawing of the scene with no text)? Answer yes if you can see ANY printed number or word, no if there is none. Answer yes or no only.
reference.qa_cell: This is ONE panel cut out of a picture-book strip. Three people stand side by side in this panel and one of them is holding a YELLOW PARCEL. What colour coat is the person holding the yellow parcel wearing? Answer with just one word from this list: red, green, brown, blue, white. If this panel does not show anybody holding a parcel at all, answer the single word missing. Nothing else.
reference.qb_cell: This is ONE panel cut out of a picture-book strip. Three people stand side by side in this panel. What colour coat is the person standing furthest to the LEFT wearing? Answer with just one word from this list: red, green, brown, blue, white. If this panel does not show the people at all, answer the single word missing. Nothing else.

steps.target: the block of comic panels itself -- the outer edge of the whole row or grid of drawn panels, counting all of the panels together as one single block; not one panel on its own, and not the paper margin, table or wall around the strip
